name: Delegation (Subagents)
description: Use subagents well — fan out independent research and verification in parallel, pick explore vs general, inherit the session's model, and avoid parallel-edit conflicts
---

# Delegating work to subagents

OpenCode runs subagents in their own **child sessions** with fresh context. They
work in the background; you get a report when each goes idle, and again after
later rounds. Use them when parallel work genuinely exists.

## When to fan out

Good candidates — work that is **independent** and **read-heavy**:

- Research several files/areas/modules at once ("find every caller of X",
  "how does auth work here", "what does this API expect").
- Verify while you implement: one child runs the tests/build while you edit.
- Compare approaches: ask two children for different designs, synthesize.
- Broad searches (docs + code + web) that don't depend on each other.

Bad candidates:

- Sequential work where step 2 needs step 1's result.
- Trivial one-liners (a child's fresh context costs tokens for no gain).
- **Parallel edits in the same tree** — see safety below.

## `explore` vs `general`

| agent | mode | use for |
|---|---|---|
| `explore` | subagent, read-only | searches, reading code/docs, answering "where/what" — cannot edit |
| `general` | subagent, broad tools | multi-step research or implementation chunks; cannot launch its own subagents |

Rule of thumb: **`explore` for questions, `general` for work**.

## Model

- A subagent **inherits the parent session's model when no model is configured** —
  so simply **omit `model`** on subagent definitions you want on the session model.
- The V2 parent can override a subagent's configured model at dispatch time
  (highest priority). If you want this enforced regardless of config, the community
  plugin `opencode-subagent-model-selector` routes by the primary session's model/variant.

## Safety before delegating

- **Scope tightly**: one clear deliverable, explicit files/paths, "report
  file:line evidence", and what *not* to touch.
- **No concurrent edits to the same tree** without worktree isolation — two
  children editing overlapping files will conflict. For parallel editing, use
  `opencode-workflows` (git worktrees per agent) or serialize the edits.
- Children inherit permissions from their own agent config, not yours; the parent's
  `subagent` permission decides which agents it may launch.
- Ask for evidence (commands run, output) — subagent claims are not verification.

## Reporting

- Mirror delegation in the progress tree: one child `progress` entry per
  delegated workstream (`parentId` = the phase), updated when the subagent reports.
- The completion notification is your cue — do not poll the child.

## Related community plugins

- `opencode-workflows` — scripted parallel subagents, worktree isolation, resume.
- `opencode-smart-subagents` — two-way messages between child and parent, batching.
- `opencode-agent-tree` — enforces decomposition into many small parallel subagents.
- `opencode-subagent-model-selector` — routes subagent models by the session model.

name: OSC 9;4 Demo
description: Demo OSC 9;4 terminal progress support in progress-tool — run a fake build that streams native OSC 9;4 progress sequences through the out-of-band relay (progress-relay), zero agent tokens
---

# OSC 9;4 demo

Run the demo and explain what the viewer sees:

1. Optionally, start the GUI first in a second terminal: `./launch-gui.sh` (from
   the progress-tool repository root — clone it to run the demos; this skill
   ships both in-repo and packaged with the plugin).
2. Run the demo: `bash demo/osc-demo.sh` (also works from any directory; set
   `PROGRESS_STATE_PATH` to isolate the state file if needed).
3. Report the outcome: the fake build emits `OSC 9;4` sequences
   (`ESC ] 9;4;<state>;<progress> BEL`), the relay parses them before text
   heuristics (state 1 → percent, state 3 → indeterminate, state 4 → waiting),
   writes throttled telemetry to the shared state file at zero token cost, and
   maps the exit code to `done`/`error`. The task `osc-demo` ends done at 100%.
4. Never poll or sleep to refresh the indicator — that is the whole point of
   the out-of-band relay.

For the full contract, see `docs/out-of-band-relay-spec.md` §6.3.1. For the
corresponding test coverage, see the "OSC 9;4" tests in
`mcp-server/test/smoke.test.js` (`cd mcp-server && npm test`).

name: Progress Tool Usage
description: Use the progress-tool MCP correctly — report long-horizon work (research, planning, exploration, refactors, docs) with the fire-and-forget progress tool, structure multi-step plans as a parentId tree, keep entries current between tool calls, and wrap long-running commands with the out-of-band progress-relay at zero token cost
---

# Using the progress tool well

The `progress` tool (progress-server MCP) is **dual purpose**:

1. **Drop-in replacement for todo/task-tracking tools** (`todowrite` / `TaskCreate`):
   any multi-step plan belongs in this tree, where it also drives the user's
   live indicator.
2. **A wrapper for long-running programmatic tool calls** (build scripts,
   compilers, test suites, installs — anything that reports progress on
   stdout) via the out-of-band relay.

## When to report

Anything expected to run **longer than a couple of minutes or a single reply** —
including work with no shell command at all: research, planning, codebase
exploration, multi-file refactors, documentation.

- **Start:** one call with `status: "running"`, a clean stable `id`
  (e.g. `"build-1"` — never session-prefixed), short `title`; put detail in
  `detail`, not the title.
- **Keep it current while you work:** non-shell work has no relay, so spend
  one of your turns **between tool calls** — roughly every few calls, or
  whenever you start or finish a step — on an update (fresh `detail`, a
  `progress: 0.0–1.0` fraction, or a status change). This todowrite-style
  cadence keeps the summary rollup live.
- **Re-arm:** when your current tree is `done` and new work begins, open a
  **fresh tree**. And if you have already made 2+ consecutive edits or shell
  calls on one task with no active entry, that **is** multi-step work —
  start a tree now (never too late: record what is done and what remains).
- **Steering is work:** when the user redirects you mid-flight while a tree
  is in progress, record the steer as a child entry — one line summarizing
  the ask plus what you plan to do in reaction — and update it as you
  respond. The user should see their steer land in the rollup.
- **Why this tool exists:** the transcript — thought traces, tool calls,
  command output — is a wall of text. The tree is the glance-able layer above
  it: a live, high-level view of what you are doing, what you are waiting on,
  and what is next. Keep it accurate at that level — a short headline title,
  the current step in `detail`, an honest `progress` fraction — so the user
  can read the pill instead of scrolling the log.
- **Close:** end with `status: "done"` or `"error"`. **Close what you open** —
  an abandoned `running` entry is a zombie the user has to dismiss by hand.
- Statuses are exactly `running | waiting | done | error` (use `waiting` for
  "not started yet / blocked"; there is no `pending`).

## Structure multi-step plans as a tree

One child entry per step — `progress({ id: "<parent>-step-1", status:
"running", title: "<step>", parentId: "<parent>" })` — then update each child
as you go. The parent's status/progress roll up automatically (error beats
running beats waiting; parent progress = mean of children). **Never embed a
numbered step list inside one title/detail** — the rollup cannot see
individual steps inside text.

## Long-running shell commands: use the relay

Call `progress` once (`status: "running"`), then run the command **through**
the out-of-band relay instead of waiting on it:

```sh
progress-relay --id <id> -- <cmd>     # wrap: exit 0 → done, non-zero → error
<cmd> | progress-relay --id <id>      # pipe: done on EOF
```

Use the exact relay command printed in the `progress` tool response (it
guarantees a working invocation path). When the harness supports background
commands, run the wrapped command in the background and keep working; the
completion notification is your cue for the final milestone.

The relay parses `OSC 9;4` terminal progress sequences (Gradle rich console,
mise, PowerShell 7.4+, …) before text heuristics like `"45%"`, and streams
throttled telemetry into the indicator at **zero token cost**.

## Never poll

No `sleep` loops, no re-calling `progress` on a timer for elapsed time or
percentages, no reading terminal output in a loop. Between-turn updates during
non-shell work are the intended cadence, not polling. The relay's exit code
maps to done/error automatically — do not re-call `progress` with `"done"`
unless adding semantic detail.

## See it live

- `bash demo/osc-demo.sh` — OSC 9;4 structured progress through the relay.
- `bash demo/tree-demo.sh` — nested parent/child roll-up
  (`PROGRESS_TREE_DEMO_FAIL=1` shows error roll-up).
- Full contract: `docs/out-of-band-relay-spec.md`.

# Task tree demo

Run the demo and explain what the viewer sees:

1. Optionally, start the GUI first in a second terminal: `./launch-gui.sh` (from
   the progress-tool repository root — clone it to run the demos; this skill
   ships both in-repo and packaged with the plugin).
2. Run the happy path: `bash demo/tree-demo.sh` (works from any directory; set
   `PROGRESS_STATE_PATH` to isolate the state file if needed).
3. Run the failure mode: `PROGRESS_TREE_DEMO_FAIL=1 bash demo/tree-demo.sh` —
   `test-e2e` fails and the error rolls up through its parent to `tree-demo`.
4. Explain the mechanics: child tasks are real background commands wrapped in
   `progress-relay` (exit code → done/error, output → detail/percent at zero
   token cost); the parent is created once with `parentId`-linked children and
   its status/progress are a read-time roll-up (error beats running beats
   waiting; parent progress = mean of child progress), per
   `docs/out-of-band-relay-spec.md` §5.6.
5. Never poll or sleep to refresh the indicator — the tree converges on its own.

For OSC 9;4 structured progress (orthogonal feature), see the `osc-demo` skill.

# @jakedowns/progress-tool-opencode-plugin

OpenCode plugin that gives agents a **fire-and-forget progress tool** and an
**out-of-band relay** for long-running commands — a live, glance-able tree above
the transcript, at zero model tokens for telemetry.

## Install

```bash
opencode plugin add @jakedowns/progress-tool-opencode-plugin
```

Restart the service (or reload the window) and a progress pill appears above the
composer. The plugin also installs and registers the MCP server
(`@jakedowns/progress-tool-mcp`) automatically, and ships four skills
(`progress-tool`, `delegation`, `osc-demo`, `tree-demo`).

The MCP entrypoint is spawned with a real JavaScript runtime (`node`, then
`bun`, then `npx -y @jakedowns/progress-tool-mcp`). It deliberately never uses
`process.execPath`, which is the `opencode` binary in OpenCode Desktop. If no
runtime is found, auto-registration is skipped with a warning, and the progress
rules / strict-mode nudges stay off until the `progress` tool is actually
available to the model. Pin a runtime with
`{ "options": { "mcpRuntime": "/absolute/path/to/node" } }` if detection picks
the wrong one.

Prefer manual configuration? Add to `opencode.json`:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": ["@jakedowns/progress-tool-opencode-plugin"],
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "progress-server": {
        "type": "local",
        "command": ["npx", "-y", "@jakedowns/progress-tool-mcp"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## What it does

- **`progress` tool** — dual purpose: a drop-in replacement for todo/task
  trackers (tree of tasks, parent/child roll-up) *and* a milestone reporter.
- **`list` tool** — read-only view of your session's trees (dismissed hidden).
- **`progress-relay`** — wraps long commands so stdout/stderr drive the UI
  (`progress-relay --id build-1 -- npm run build`); exit code maps to
  done/error. Parses `OSC 9;4` progress sequences natively.
- **Desktop pill** — `(N · agg%)` title, collapsible trees (animated),
  dismissals that persist, started/last-updated tooltips, nudge telemetry.
- **Guidance that adapts** — injected rules, skill playbooks, pre-flight relay
  hints, strict-mode nudges (silent runs, stale progress), a turn-end idle
  reminder, and an optional 2-minute wall-clock nudge.

## Options

Pass under the plugin entry's `options` in `opencode.json`:

| option | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `injectInstructions` | `true` | inject progress/relay rules into every session |
| `registerSkills` | `true` | register the bundled skills |
| `autoRegisterMcp` | `true` | register `@jakedowns/progress-tool-mcp` automatically |
| `mcpRuntime` | auto | absolute path to the `node`/`bun` used to spawn the MCP server (auto-detected; set this if detection picks wrong) |
| `strictMode` | `"nudge"` | `"nudge"` / `"force"` / `"off"` tool-call monitor |
| `wallClockMs` | `120000` | wall-clock nudge threshold (`0` disables) |
| `idleReminder` | `true` | turn-end nudge when open tasks remain |
| `unhinged` | `false` | append a task-list reminder to every user message |
| `verboseLogging` | `false` | JSONL nudge telemetry (`~/.opencode-progress-nudges.log`) |
| `autoHideDone` | `false` | hide completed tasks after the success hold |
| `expandRootsByDefault` | `false` | expand pill tree roots by default |
| `barStyle` | `"blocks"` | `"blocks"` or `"emoji"` |
| `refreshMs` | `1000` | view refresh interval |

State lives in `~/.opencode-progress-state.json` (override with
`PROGRESS_STATE_PATH`). Retention is opt-in (`PROGRESS_AUTO_PRUNE_S`); entries
ride by default so the store doubles as a report.
